name: Cayman Islands

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Department of Commerce and Investment quotes the trade and business licence fee for your activity. Micro businesses (up to four employees and CI$250,000 in yearly revenue) pay reduced fees.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a sole trader business. The General Registry quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: Search the name at the General Registry first.

launchSteps.label: Incorporate the company at the General Registry
launchSteps.plain: Only needed for a limited company. A sole trader does not incorporate.

launchSteps.label: Apply for your trade and business licence
launchSteps.plain: Every business needs one before it starts trading. You apply through the Department of Commerce and Investment, and renew it every year. Micro and small businesses get reduced fees.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Set up pension and health insurance for your employees
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay 5% pension contributions (matched by the employee) and at least half of each employee's health insurance premium. Non-Caymanian staff also need a work permit.

calendar.monthlyText: With employees: pay pension contributions to your registered pension plan by the 15th of the following month.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: Renew your trade and business licence.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay the pension contributions of the previous month, and keep each employee's health insurance premium paid.

notes: The Cayman Islands has no income tax, no corporate tax and no sales tax. Your main costs are the trade and business licence, import duty on goods you bring in and, with employees, pension and health insurance.
With employees you pay at least half of each premium for their health insurance: ask an insurer for a quote, because it is not included in your estimate.
